review: מוֹלַדְתִּי is the fixed refrain word for وَطَنِي in every stanza; it is the biblical אֶרֶץ מוֹלַדְתּוֹ (Gen 11:28) and carries the exile/home tension better than אַרְצִי.
1:3 תּוֹשָׁב — 'sojourner', biblical (Gen 23:4 גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב אָנֹכִי עִמָּכֶם); the line is deliberately built on that verse.
3:1 הִנְנִי אֹרֵחַ וּפוֹנֶה — 'behold, I am a wayfarer turning [my face]'; the Arabic سَائِحٌ قَاصِدٌ has no single Hebrew equivalent, so the two participles carry it.
5:2 אֲשֶׁר נָחַנִי — 'who guided me'; the same root as תַּנְחֵנִי in tr0015, kept for consistency across the book.
